memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'and take it to Aaron's sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.'" - Lev 2:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Only a handful goes on the fire. The rest stays behind. And yet that single handful is called a memorial portion — the part that represents the whole.

The Hebrew word suggests remembrance. This small burning handful was a reminder before God of the whole offering, and of the person who brought it. God does not need reminding the way we do, but He chose to build into Israel's worship a picture of being remembered by Him.

Think about what that meant to an ordinary farmer. He was one of hundreds of thousands. He would never speak to Moses. He would likely never be named in any record. But a handful of his flour went up in smoke before the God of the universe, and it stood as a memorial that this man had come.

You are not lost in the crowd before God. Cornelius was told that his prayers and gifts had come up as a memorial offering before God (Acts 10:4) — the same idea, carried straight into the New Testament. God notices the small, quiet, unwitnessed things you bring Him.

And once again the chapter closes its instruction with that phrase from chapter 1: an aroma pleasing to the LORD. God is not indifferent to what you offer. He receives it with pleasure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God notices the small offerings nobody else sees?
2. Whose quiet, faithful service around me could I encourage today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that nothing I bring You is lost or overlooked. Let even the smallest offering of my life rise as a memorial before You. Amen.
